stories.summary: Rate-limit the remote MCP bearer gate per client and per subject
stories.description: The remote MCP transport has no rate limiting at the gate: unbounded token-guessing and unbounded authenticated tool calls.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83 - a stand-in of RMH-01 and RMH-02 together (per-IP failed-auth and per-subject request buckets with 429 in BearerAuthMiddleware, defaults 10 and 120 per minute; can_view in app/policy.py; a pre-call visibility check for plan-scoped read tools in remote_tool_policy): 17747 passed / 21 skipped, 0 conflicts (no existing test sends more than ten failed authentications per minute or calls a read tool on a plan the remote principal does not own). Four other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is the root user's home, which the guard bans by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary).

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHAT TO BUILD in pipeline/remote_transport.py `BearerAuthMiddleware` (helpers may go in a new pipeline/rate_limit.py to keep the middleware readable):
1. A token bucket per client address for FAILED authentications (`PIPELINE_MCP_AUTH_FAIL_PER_MIN`, default 10) checked BEFORE token verification, so a blocked client costs no JWKS work; and a bucket per authenticated subject for requests (`PIPELINE_MCP_REQUESTS_PER_MIN`, default 120).
2. Over the limit: HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` and the correlation-id header, the same JSON error shape the 401 path uses, no detail about the limit state.
3. Values: positive integers; `0` disables that bucket explicitly; anything else (negative, non-integer) refuses to start the transport with an error naming the variable (fail closed).
4. Record the FIRST rejection per client/subject per window in the host audit chain (`append_host_audit`, action `mcp:rate_limited`), not every rejection.
5. Client address (decided - this is the security-critical part): `_client_ip` returns the raw ASGI peer, which behind a reverse proxy is the PROXY, so every client would share one failed-auth bucket and one attacker could lock everyone out. Add `PIPELINE_MCP_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (comma-separated IPs/CIDRs, parsed with `ipaddress`; malformed -> refuse to start). Empty (the default) keys on the peer, as today. When the peer is in the trusted set, key on the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry that is NOT in the trusted set; a missing or malformed header falls back to the peer. Never trust `X-Forwarded-For` from an untrusted peer.
Buckets are in-process memory; document that a multi-replica deployment needs a shared limiter (out of scope).

DOCS: REFERENCE.md "Remote MCP transport" section - rewrite the bullet that begins "There is **no rate limiting** at the gate" (it is false after this story) and add the three variables to its configuration rows; docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md "Remote MCP transport hardening" row.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_remote_mcp_rate_limit.py, driving the ASGI middleware directly with a fake clock): 11th failed auth in a minute -> 429 without calling the provider; bucket refills after the window; authenticated subject over limit -> 429, another subject unaffected; 0 disables; invalid values refuse startup; one host-audit record per window; 429 body carries no token or limit internals; with no trusted proxies a spoofed X-Forwarded-For is ignored; with the proxy trusted, two clients behind it get separate buckets; a malformed CIDR refuses startup.

GENERAL RULES (every step of this story):
- Write the failing tests first (CLAUDE.md Step 3) and confirm they fail on an assertion, not an import error.
- Verify with the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; all must be green before you finish. Report pass/fail counts in the PR description.
- A new test file that imports any `pipeline.*` module must `import pipeline.server` first (pre-existing import cycle). Copy the idiom in tests/unit/test_triage_cap_silent_skip.py.
- Bind a non-operator principal in tests the way tests/unit/test_patch_plan_enforcement.py does (`pipeline.actor.bind_principal`); never add an `actor` parameter to any MCP tool (a guard test forbids it).
- The harness scratchpad `.agent_scratchpad.md` stays untracked. Commit only the files this brief names plus the new test files it asks for. Add no helper scripts, dumps or module copies.
- Never modify an existing test except as this brief pre-authorizes, with the literal edit given. If another pre-existing test fails because of a change this brief requires, do NOT undo the required change - stop and report the conflict, naming the test and the requirement it contradicts.
- Comments and docs you write must stay true after later stories merge: state the invariant, never "until story X lands".
- Cumulative artifacts (the REFERENCE.md policy table, the IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 rows, `REMOTE_*` sets): assert only what YOU add or remove (membership/absence), never the full contents, an exact count, or a hash.
- Error messages and logs name the action and the principal subject only - never a token, secret, payload, path or exception text (Secure-by-Design).
- Commit message: Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, subject <=72 chars), body explains why; put the story key in the body. If you change an existing test as pre-authorized, the body must say which test and why (CLAUDE.md Step 4).

stories.summary: Scope remote read tools to the plans a principal owns or is delegated
stories.description: The six remote read tools are not tenant-scoped: any remote caller sees every plan, its stories, decisions and diffs.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83 - a stand-in of RMH-01 and RMH-02 together (per-IP failed-auth and per-subject request buckets with 429 in BearerAuthMiddleware, defaults 10 and 120 per minute; can_view in app/policy.py; a pre-call visibility check for plan-scoped read tools in remote_tool_policy): 17747 passed / 21 skipped, 0 conflicts (no existing test sends more than ten failed authentications per minute or calls a read tool on a plan the remote principal does not own). WHAT TO BUILD:
1. app/policy.py: `can_view(principal, resource) -> bool`, deny by default: the local operator sees everything; a principal sees a plan it owns or is a delegate of; everything else, including an un-owned plan, is invisible to a remote principal. Fail closed on any error (reuse `is_allowed`'s pattern).
2. pipeline/remote_tool_policy.py `remote_tool_policy` middleware (every caller there is remote; the local-identity case is already refused):
   - Plan-scoped read tools (`check_story_status`, `get_story_diff`, `list_decisions`, `list_ready_stories`): BEFORE `call_next`, read `plan_name` from `ctx.params["arguments"]`, load the manifest with `pipeline.authorization._load_manifest`, build the resource with `resource_for`, and when `can_view` is False return one fixed `isError` result whose text is identical for a plan that does not exist and a plan the caller may not see (no existence oracle); record it in the host chain as `tool:call` outcome `hidden`.
   - `list_plans` returns raw file stems of PLAN_DIR (`<plan>`, `<plan>.manifest`, sidecar stems - see its docstring in pipeline/server.py). After `call_next`, drop every stem whose plan (the stem up to its first `.`) is not visible. Mirror how tests/unit/test_remote_tool_policy.py drives the middleware with a fake ctx/call_next to learn the result object's shape in this SDK version; do not re-implement the tool.
   - `check_usage` stays host-level and unfiltered; `verify_audit` (AA-01, if merged) is filtered like `list_plans`: drop invisible plans' entries, and drop the `host` entry for every remote caller (the host chain records other principals' authentication attempts). State each choice in the module docstring, and update the `REMOTE_READ` comment that says the tools "are not tenant-scoped yet".

DOCS: docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md "Remote MCP transport hardening" row and REFERENCE.md remote transport section - replace "These are **not tenant-scoped**: any remote caller sees every plan they list." with the scoping rule.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_remote_read_scoping.py): owner sees own plan only in list_plans; delegate sees it; stranger sees none and gets the identical hidden response for a known plan and an unknown one (byte-equal result text); local operator sees all; un-owned plan invisible remotely; policy exception -> invisible.
